title: Hardship and Protective Holds: Letter Turnaround and the Initial Service Documentation Due Date
content:
**Ruling.** On a Military Service Hold request under Hardship and Protective Holds, the point the initial service documentation is counted from depends on how many calendar days after the request date the request letter is sent:

1. More than the late-send days of 7 after the request date: the documentation is due the tier's documentation days, 30 calendar days, after the day the letter is sent.
2. More than the tier's decision days of 3, counted as calendar days, but no more than 7 after the request date: it is due those 3 decision days, again counted as calendar days, plus the 30 documentation days — that is 33 calendar days — after the request date.
3. Otherwise (3 days or fewer after the request date): it is due 30 calendar days after the request date.

The days allowed for the initial service documentation are the calendar days from the day the letter is sent to the due date so found.

## Day-by-day table

| Letter sent, days after the request date | Due date | Days allowed |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Request date plus 30 | 30 |
| 2 | Request date plus 30 | 28 |
| 3 | Request date plus 30 | 27 |
| 4 | Request date plus 33 | 29 |
| 7 | Request date plus 33 | 26 |
| 8 | Letter date plus 30 | 30 |
| 12 | Letter date plus 30 | 30 |

## Dated case (hypothetical)

A request was received on 2 June and the letter goes out on 7 June, 5 days later — more than 3, no more than 7. The documentation is due 33 days after 2 June, on 5 July; from 7 June that is 28 days allowed.
